topic: Lambda Variadics for Arbitrary Argument Forwarding (C++14)
explanation: C++14 extended generic lambdas to support variadic templates, allowing them to accept and process an arbitrary number of arguments using a parameter pack (`... params`). Combined with `decltype`-based perfect forwarding, this enables the creation of fully generic wrapper functions that can perfectly forward arguments to any underlying function call, regardless of the number or type of parameters.
practical_example: A library requires logging every call to an internal processing function. A single C++14 variadic lambda is used as a wrapper, logging the call and then perfectly forwarding the entire parameter pack to the original function, minimizing boilerplate code for different function signatures.
keywords: Variadic lambda, generic lambda forwarding, lambda perfect forwarding, C++14 variadic
chapter: Item 33: Use decltype on auto&& parameters to std::forward them
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
